module.purpose: Provides a utility function to create derived atoms by selecting a slice from a parent atom's value with three-level WeakMap memoization caching.
module.summary: This file implements selectAtom, a function that creates a derived atom by applying a selector function to extract a slice from a parent atom's value. It uses a three-level WeakMap-based memoization cache (memo3) to optimize performance by caching based on the atom, selector function, and equality function dependencies. The implementation includes careful handling of initialization with an EMPTY symbol sentinel and supports custom equality comparison for slice values.
module.businessContext: Enables efficient derived state computation in reactive atom-based state management systems. Critical for performance when selecting subsets of large atom values.
functions: getCached (~L4-5): Generic cache retrieval with lazy initialization
memo3 (~L9-18): Three-level dependency memoization using WeakMaps
selectAtom (~L20-59): Creates derived atom with selector-based slicing

units.name: getCached
units.source:
const getCached = <T>(c: () => T, m: WeakMap<object, unknown>, k: object): T =>
  (m.has(k) ? m : m.set(k, c())).get(k) as T

detail.name: getCached
detail.signature: <T>(c: () => T, m: WeakMap<object, unknown>, k: object): T
preconditions: The WeakMap 'm' must be capable of holding object keys.
The factory function 'c' must return a value of type T.
The key 'k' must be a valid object (not null or a primitive).
postconditions: The returned value is of type T.
If the key was present in 'm' on entry, the value returned is the same object instance that was stored.
If the key was not present, the factory function 'c' is called exactly once, its return value is stored in 'm' for key 'k', and the same value is returned.
invariants: The WeakMap 'm' may be mutated only when 'k' is not already present in it.
The function is referentially transparent for the same key 'k' within the same WeakMap 'm' instance, modulo WeakMap garbage collection.
edgeCases: If 'k' is already in 'm', the factory 'c' is not invoked.
If 'k' is not in 'm', the factory 'c' is called and its result is stored.
If 'c' throws, the exception propagates and no entry is added to 'm'.
If 'm' is a WeakMap that has cleared the entry for 'k' (e.g., due to garbage collection), the factory will be called again.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: No explicit error handling; passes invalid inputs to WeakMap operations which may throw.

stateMutations: WeakMap 'm' is mutated (via 'set') when 'k' is not already present.

detail.name: memo3
detail.signature: function memo3<T>(create: () => T, dep1: object, dep2: object, dep3: object): T
preconditions: dep1, dep2, dep3 must be non-null object references (valid WeakMap keys)
create must be a callable that returns a value of type T
postconditions: Returns a cached value of type T
When all three dependency references are identical to a prior call, the create function is not invoked and the previously returned value is returned again
When any dependency reference changes, a new cache path is followed and create may be invoked
invariants: Cache is keyed by object reference identity (===), not structural equality
Cache entries are held weakly via WeakMap and do not prevent garbage collection of dependency objects
edgeCases: Same object references passed repeatedly always return the same cached T instance
A previously-seen dep1 with a new dep2 will reuse the second-level cache from the first-level but traverse a different third-level entry
If any dependency is garbage-collected, its WeakMap entry becomes eligible for cleanup
stateMutations: Writes into the module-level WeakMap cache1 under dep1
Writes into intermediate WeakMaps (cache2, cache3) for new dependency combinations
detail.summary: Three-level memoization utility that caches the result of a factory function based on three object-reference dependencies, using nested WeakMaps so that identical object references at every level return the previously computed result without re-invoking the factory.

specTests.then: The second call returns a different result (create invoked again) because dep3 differs by reference

detail.name: selectAtom
detail.signature: export function selectAtom<Value, Slice>(anAtom: Atom<Value>, selector: (v: Value, prevSlice?: Slice) => Slice, equalityFn?: (a: Slice, b: Slice) => boolean): Atom<Slice>
preconditions: anAtom must be a valid Atom<Value> instance
selector must be a function that maps Value to Slice; on first read prevSlice will be undefined
equalityFn, if provided, must be a pure function comparing two Slice values for equality
postconditions: Returns an Atom<Slice> whose value is the result of applying selector to the source atom's value
On first read, selector is called with only the value (prevSlice is undefined)
On subsequent reads, selector is called with both value and prevSlice
When equalityFn(prevSlice, newSlice) is true, the previous slice reference is returned unchanged
When equalityFn(prevSlice, newSlice) is false, the new slice is returned
invariants: The derived atom's value is always equal to selector(sourceValue) or a previously returned slice reference when equal
Memoization ensures that identical (anAtom, selector, equalityFn) inputs return the same derived atom instance
edgeCases: First read before any source atom value is set: selector is called with (value, undefined) — prevSlice is undefined because the EMPTY sentinel is not exposed to the selector
Selector returns the same reference: equalityFn comparison short-circuits and prevSlice is returned, maintaining referential stability
Selector returns a structurally equal but referentially different object: behavior depends entirely on the equalityFn; with default Object.is the new reference is returned
Selector throws: the error propagates from the derived atom's read
stateMutations: Creates and registers a new derived atom (via memo3) in the internal memoization cache
The derived atom's init property is set to the EMPTY sentinel as a read-before-init hack
detail.summary: Derives a new atom that selects a slice from a source atom's value, preserving referential stability by returning the previous slice reference when the equality function determines the new and old slices are equal.

specLiterals.role: EMPTY sentinel used to detect first-read vs subsequent-read state in the derived atom; not exposed to caller but defines the internal state machine
